course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Angles and Constructions
unit.blurb: Angles at a point, angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles, angles in a triangle and quadrilateral, and accurate drawing of lines and quadrilaterals.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Know that angles at a point add up to 360° and use this to find missing angles.

O2.t: Recognise angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles and the angles of a triangle, and find missing angles.

O3.t: Draw parallel and perpendicular lines and construct quadrilaterals accurately with a ruler and protractor.

p: A full turn is **360°**. Angles that meet at a point and fill the full turn **add up to 360°**.
The angles inside any **quadrilateral** also add up to 360° (it splits into two triangles of 180°).

p: Angles on a straight line make 180°; angles all the way round a point make 360°.

p: Angles on a **straight line** add up to **180°**.
When two lines cross, the opposite angles are equal: these are **vertically opposite angles**.
The angles in a **triangle** add up to **180°**.
Vertically opposite angles are across the crossing point, not next to each other (those add to 180°).

p: **Parallel** lines stay the same distance apart and never meet (marked with arrows). **Perpendicular** lines meet at a **right angle** (90°).
To draw a quadrilateral accurately, use a ruler for lengths (to the nearest mm) and a protractor for angles (to the nearest degree).
A protractor has two scales. Start from 0° on the line you are measuring from.
